title: european refiners reaping near record profits gasoline 2026 09 02
text:
LONDON, Sept 2 (Reuters) - European gasoline refinery profit margins passed $62 a ​barrel on Wednesday, according to trade ‌data reviewed by Reuters, driven higher as conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine ​tighten fuel supplies globally.
Eurobob E5 physical ​gasoline barges were trading at a ⁠premium to Brent futures of about $62.07 ​a barrel around 1420 GMT, according to ​price data from LSEG and market participants, up from a $55.62 premium on Tuesday.
Wednesday's refining margin is ​just short of the $62.10 record high ​Eurobob E5 gasoline margins reached in June 2022 ‌at ⁠the height of oil price disruptions after the start of the war in Ukraine.
Global refined fuel markets have been tightened ​this year ​by ⁠attacks on refineries in the Middle East and Russia, while ​in North West Europe a hot ​and ⁠dry summer drove down water levels on the Rhine river, hampering barge traffic ⁠into ​the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) hub where ​Eurobob barges trade.
